analysis: Examined the two changed files. (1) provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDBlockStore.swift readExactly (patch hunk @@ -481 / head lines ~493-501): removes the upfront reserveCapacity(count) and, when the first read returns exactly `count` bytes with startIndex == 0, returns that buffer directly instead of appending into a second Data. When the first chunk is shorter, it reserves capacity then appends as before. The `beforeRead` budget hooks, EOF/truncation check (throws if chunk is nil before count satisfied), and loop bound are unchanged. The sole behavioral change is the avoided copy. I identified no change to authentication, AES-GCM chunk/tag verification, identity binding, HMAC lookup tags, the read-byte accounting (beforeRead(count) is still called before the read), or on-disk format. The startIndex == 0 guard addresses slice-index hazards for callers indexing from zero. A residual question is whether the returned Data could be a slice sharing a larger backing buffer, which would retain more memory. The guard chunk.count == count means the buffer size equals the span, and the reader source is not in the supplied evidence. Memory-accounting impact against the provider ledger (TB-007, T-041 e) is therefore likely neutral or beneficial. Plaintext lifetime in decrypted/authenticated paths is unchanged in kind, since readExactly handles raw file fields, not new plaintext exposure. (2) docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: the date bump and the Streaming-read row describe the readExactly behavior. The rest of the file is unchanged context, consistent with T-041 (TTL 1800, HMAC tags, KEK custody). No new attack surface, threat-model assumption invalidation, or doc/threat-model gap was identified. Unverified: the readExactly callers and the chunk-read primitive (SSDNoFollowIO) are not supplied, so zero-index and slice semantics are assumed from the code comment.
